message.content: **Summary:** I researched Apple's latest results and bought 44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $223.00 (filled at $223.00, ~$9,812 total — under the $10,000 per-order cap and well within the $20,000 daily limit, with no funds moved out of the account). The decision rested on Apple's fiscal 2024 results reported October 31: Q4 revenue of $94.9B, up 6% year over year, and full-year net sales of $391.0B (up from $383.3B), operating income of $123.2B, net income of $93.7B, and diluted EPS of $6.08 — the latter depressed by a one-time $10.2B tax charge, meaning underlying earnings power is better than the headline figure suggests. The stock was trading around $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72) with shares described as little changed as investors weigh iPhone 16 demand and the gradual Apple Intelligence rollout, so my limit was set essentially at market rather than chasing a move. One caution: a search result claiming Apple guided FY25 to $9.50 EPS and >25% revenue growth came from an unverified site and is not credible (it would imply ~56% EPS growth off a $6.08 base), so I excluded it from my reasoning and relied only on Apple's newsroom release and the SEC 10-K.
